headline: Fuel and pork rebound powers a sharp earnings turnaround
summary_short: Net sales rose to $2,400M (+3.6% y/y) as a $76M jump in Liquid Fuels revenue offset roughly flat Pork and lower CT&M/Marine sales; operating income surged to $96M (+152.6% y/y, +47.7% q/q) and net income of $119M was up 271.9% y/y but down 53.0% from Q4 2025.
summary_long: Liquid Fuels operating income swung to $37M from -$26M on higher renewable-diesel margins and volumes plus $12M more production tax credits; Pork improved to $7M from -$31M on lower legal-claims expense and feed costs. CT&M fell to $17M from $41M on mark-to-market derivative losses; Marine fell to $34M from $57M on lower freight rates and higher voyage costs. Operating cash outflow widened to $54M from $20M on an $111M working-capital build, mainly Liquid Fuels inventory. Cash plus short-term investments totaled $1,161M; long-term debt was $974M. No shares were repurchased this quarter ($62M remains available); the dividend held at $2.25/share. Management budgets roughly $460M of FY2026 capex, including ~$125M for the Power segment's new barge.

drivers.explanation: Operating income rose sharply on higher Liquid Fuels and Pork margins, partly offset by CT&M mark-to-market losses and lower Marine freight rates; Turkey/Butterball equity income also improved.
Net sales rose $84M y/y, primarily $76M higher Liquid Fuels sales on increased volumes of fuel sold.

Gross profit is the arithmetic difference between reported Revenue ($2,400M) and Cost of revenue ($2,183M), both SEC-verbatim lines; the filing presents no consolidated gross-profit subtotal of its own.

Operating income rose $58M y/y: +$63M Liquid Fuels (fuel margins, production tax credits) and +$38M Pork (lower legal-claims expense, feed costs), partly offset by -$24M CT&M (mark-to-market losses) and -$23M Marine (freight rates, voyage costs).
Net income rose $87M y/y on higher operating income and $24M more Turkey/Butterball equity income versus near-zero a year ago; the filing does not address the q/q comparison to Q4 2025.
Diluted EPS rose in line with net income growth on a slightly smaller weighted diluted share count (957,794 vs 971,055 shares a year ago).

Cash used in operations grew to $54M from $20M, mainly on $111M more cash used for working capital (Liquid Fuels inventory build), partly offset by higher net earnings and $21M more affiliate dividends received.
